dedupe_keys.name: c40 infrastructure interdependencies and climate risks report 2017 amsterdam bogota johannesburg melbourne and toronto

description: This C40 report, published in spring 2017, examines how city governments work with the owners of energy, transport, telecommunications, water and wastewater, solid waste and food infrastructure to understand interdependencies and the cascading effects of climate change on them. It was commissioned by the C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group, conceived by staff in Toronto and Amsterdam, and draws on detailed cases from Amsterdam, Bogotá, Johannesburg, Melbourne and Toronto with operators such as Toronto Hydro, Enbridge, Enwave, Alliander, the Amsterdam Internet Exchange and Melbourne Water. It covers initial engagement, interactive workshops to map interdependencies, maps of climate exposure, vulnerability and risk assessments, failure points that lead to cascading impacts, data sharing between agencies and operators, and examples of collaborative risk reduction, closing with best practices. Coverage is five cities on five continents, with other examples mostly from North America. Format and access: a 56-page PDF hosted by the UNFCCC. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: the cases are qualitative and self-reported by the cities. It informs climate adaptation planning and cascading failure studies of urban infrastructure networks. Related catalogue records are the inter 3 guide to KRITIS interdependency analysis and the Melbourne Coastal Adaptation Pathways Project.
